name: Yttrium-substituted bismuth strontium calcium cuprate
equilibrium_context: Tc about 96 K at optimal doping; underdoped samples with a pseudogap above Tc
summary: The most prominent cuprate WITHOUT a robust finding of photoinduced superconductivity, despite intensive study.

driven_states.emergent_property: Ultrashort near-infrared excitation in the pseudogap regime produces an anomalous decrease of the charge carrier scattering rate: antinodal excitations evolve from gapped to delocalized quasiparticles, and the optical conductivity increases. NO condensate forms.
driven_states.source: Cilento et al., Nat. Commun. 5, 4353 (2014), doi:10.1038/ncomms5353
driven_states.caveat: Explicitly NOT evidence of light-induced superconductivity, although it is occasionally miscited as such. Any Josephson plasma edge, any 1/omega divergence and any optical gap are absent. The entry is included in the registry as a corrective.

sources: Cilento et al., Nat. Commun. 5, 4353 (2014), doi:10.1038/ncomms5353
gaps: Fluence known only to order of magnitude.
